stories.title: White Sox and Rays Each Take Commanding 2-0 ALDS Leads

x_posts.label: Post 1-1
x_posts.text:
The Chicago White Sox lead the ALDS 2-0.

Three years ago they lost 121 games.

Last year they lost 102.

Now they are one win from the American League Championship Series.

This run is going to be talked about forever. ⚾

#WhiteSox #MLB

x_posts.label: Post 1-2
x_posts.text:
ALDS update:

White Sox 2-0 over Cleveland (Game 3 tomorrow)
Rays 2-0 over Yankees (Game 3 tomorrow)

Both teams one win from the ALCS.

The Rays eliminated the Yankees without Aaron Judge playing a single inning. 👀

#MLB #Playoffs

facebook.long_form:
One win from the ALCS.

The Chicago White Sox entered the 2026 season having lost at least 100 games in each of the past three years — including a record-setting 121-loss 2024 season. Their opening day playoff odds were listed at 1.1 percent. Most people didn't pick them to sniff the Wild Card. None of that matters now.

The White Sox beat the Cleveland Guardians 4-3 in ALDS Game 2 on October 5, following their 3-0 Game 1 victory on October 3. They lead the series 2-0 and need one win to advance to the American League Championship Series.

The Tampa Bay Rays are right there with them. Tampa Bay dispatched the New York Yankees 5-2 in Game 2, adding to their 1-0 Game 1 win. The Rays lead their ALDS 2-0 as well — and notably, they have done this without Aaron Judge playing a single inning of postseason baseball. Judge (right calf/soleus strain) was off the Wild Card roster and his ALDS availability has been uncertain.

Both series have Game 3 scheduled for October 7. Two teams. Two commanding leads. Two organizations telling completely different stories about how you get here.

---

stories.title: Pete Crow-Armstrong Joins Exclusive 40-40 Club — Seventh in MLB History

x_posts.label: Post 2-1
x_posts.text:
Pete Crow-Armstrong finished 2026 with 45 HR and 40 SB.

Only 7 players in MLB history have done that:
Canseco. Bonds. A-Rod. Soriano. Acuña. Ohtani.

Now Crow-Armstrong.

He's also the first Cub ever in the 40-40 club. 🐻

#Cubs #MLB

x_posts.label: Post 2-2
x_posts.text:
Pete Crow-Armstrong: 45 HR. 40 SB.

Historic season. One of 7 ever.

Then the Padres swept the Cubs in the Wild Card and he went 0-for-7.

Baseball is a sport of maximum highs and maximum lows, sometimes in the same week.

#Cubs #MLB

facebook.long_form:
Forty home runs. Forty stolen bases. In the same season.

Only six players in the history of Major League Baseball had done that before Pete Crow-Armstrong did it in 2026. The list reads like a Hall of Fame exhibit: José Canseco (1988). Barry Bonds (1996). Alex Rodriguez (1998). Alfonso Soriano (2006). Ronald Acuña Jr. (2023). Shohei Ohtani (2024).

And now: Pete Crow-Armstrong, 2026, with 45 home runs and 40 stolen bases.

He is also the first Cub in franchise history — a franchise that has existed since 1876 — to achieve a 40-40 season.

The calendar does not care about milestones. The Padres swept the Cubs 2-0 in the NL Wild Card Series that concluded October 1. Crow-Armstrong went 0-for-7 with 4 strikeouts in the two games, a jarring contrast to a regular season that placed him in genuinely elite historical company.

That is baseball. Historic regular seasons and early playoff exits can share the same October. The statistics are permanent. The 40-40 will be in the record book long after this week is forgotten.

---

facebook.long_form:
Two NLDS storylines headed into Tuesday night.

First: Milwaukee. The Brewers won Game 2 of their NLDS against the San Diego Padres on a walk-off, 4-3, and now lead the series 2-0. One win separates Milwaukee from the NLCS. Game 3 is tonight at 9:30 PM ET on FS1. The Padres made it past the Cubs in the Wild Card, but the Brewers have shown no mercy in this series.

Second: Atlanta and Los Angeles. The Braves and Dodgers are knotted 1-1 after the Braves took Game 2 in a 3-2 win. The deciding play came on a wild pitch by Dodgers pitcher Kris Bubic that allowed Michael Harris II to score from third. Chris Sale is expected to take the ball for Atlanta in tonight's Game 3 at 6:00 PM ET on FS1. The winner goes to 2-1 with a chance to close out the series Thursday. The loser faces elimination.

It is a full night of October baseball. Both NLDS matchups at critical junctures. Whoever advances from these two series will have earned it.

stories.title: 2026 Season Milestone Roundup — Skubal 1,000th K; Sánchez Phillies Record; Murakami History

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text:
2026 MLB milestones worth remembering:

Skubal: 1,000th career strikeout
Sánchez: 41⅔ scoreless IP — breaks 115-year Phillies record
Murakami: 7 HR in first 21 games (more than Ohtani)
Ramírez: HR vs. all 29 other teams

The regular season left its mark. ⚾

#MLB

facebook.long_form:
The Wild Card races and playoff runs dominated the September news cycle, but several remarkable individual milestones from the 2026 regular season deserve recognition as the curtain comes down on the regular season.

**Tarik Skubal, Detroit Tigers.** On July 29 at Baltimore, Skubal recorded the 1,000th strikeout of his MLB career. He has established himself as one of the most dominant starting pitchers in the American League — a career milestone that arrived quietly during a season full of noise elsewhere.

**Cristopher Sánchez, Philadelphia Phillies.** Sánchez extended a consecutive scoreless innings streak to 41⅔ innings, breaking a Phillies franchise record that had stood for 115 years. The previous holder: Grover Cleveland Alexander, who set the mark in 1911. To break a record that old is to find yourself in genuinely rare historical territory.

**Munetaka Murakami, Chicago White Sox.** In his first 21 MLB games, the Japanese slugger hit 7 home runs — breaking Shohei Ohtani's previous record of 5 home runs by a Japanese-born player through his first 21 games. He is now in the ALDS with a White Sox team one win from the ALCS.

**José Ramírez, Cleveland Guardians.** Ramírez became the first Guardian in franchise history to hit a home run against all 29 other MLB teams — a milestone that speaks to consistency, longevity, and the kind of performance that makes people forget to be properly amazed.

stories.title: Nootbaar to Arizona; MLB Offseason Outlook Launches

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text:
Lars Nootbaar was traded from St. Louis to Arizona on October 1.

And MLB Trade Rumors just launched its Offseason Outlook series — all 30 teams.

The postseason is happening. The front offices are already working on 2027.

Welcome to the offseason overlap. ⚾

#MLB

facebook.long_form:
The postseason is underway, but the offseason has already started for some teams.

The St. Louis Cardinals made that clear on October 1, trading Lars Nootbaar along with three pitchers — Brian Curley, Daniel Eagen, and Sandro Santana — to the Arizona Diamondbacks. The move was executed as the Wild Card round was beginning, a signal that St. Louis is already focused on what comes next rather than this October.

At the same time, MLB Trade Rumors launched its 2026-27 Offseason Outlook series on October 3 — a comprehensive preview of how all 30 teams plan to approach the coming hot stove season. It is October 6. The World Series champion won't be crowned for weeks. And already, the front office chess game for 2027 is in motion.

For teams watching the playoffs from home, the work never stops. The gap between regular season and offseason has narrowed to nearly zero. While Milwaukee and Atlanta are playing for pennant berths tonight, GM offices across the country are building their target lists, calculating luxury tax implications, and identifying which portal of available talent — free agency, trade, or extension — is the right vehicle for the changes they need to make.

The 2026 season isn't over. But the 2027 season has already started.

---
